audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty is TRICKY 7/10 with the reason given as 'front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching' — no mechanic, no number. Meanwhile the level chart (both packet and content layer) says Ahri owns levels 1-5.
audit.why: The lane is hard for exactly one window — Fizz's first item at 6+ — and easy before it, because Urchin Strike is 550 range and Playful/Trickster is 400. Nothing in his kit reaches Ahri's 970 orb or 975 charm until he commits.
audit.corrected: Difficulty grounded on his 550/400 engage ranges early and the Chum the Waters window late.
sources: brief.enemyKit Q range 550, E range 400, R range 1300

audit.whatIsWrong: Six level-chart rows disagree between layers. The full layer reads Fizz/Skill/Skill/Skill/Fizz/Skill/Skill; the content layer reads Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Fizz/Skill.
audit.why: The packet levelChart matches the content layer exactly (Ahri x5, Fizz, Skill). The full layer disagrees on six of seven rows and, worse, gives Level 1 to Fizz — the opposite of what the same page's content layer tells the reader two panels down.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side -> Ahri, phases[5].side -> Fizz, phases[6] stays Skill. Proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fizz's passive is never mentioned anywhere in either layer: he moves through units and takes a FLAT amount of reduced damage from every source.
audit.why: Flat reduction per instance is specifically bad against Fox-Fire, which is three small hits rather than one big one — a large fraction of that damage is shaved off before it lands. It is the reason poking a Fizz with W feels like it does nothing, and it changes the correct trade order to orb-first. 'Move through units' also means minions never body-block his approach.
audit.corrected: Written into tradeGood/breakdown.trading (lead with the orb, not the W) and dontsFull[0].d (the minion wall is not a wall).

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d calls Playful/Trickster a 'fifteen-second invitation' and breakdown.cooldowns says 'count it out loud if you must' without ever giving the count.
audit.why: Playful/Trickster is 16/14/12/10/8. Fifteen seconds is wrong at every rank, and by rank 5 the window is half what the page implies — an 8-second gap is not a window you plan a commit around the way you plan around 16.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written in: '16s at rank 1 down to 8s at rank 5, and untargetable throughout.'

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] and spikes[1].text both describe Chum the Waters as landing a 'root'. It is not a root — the fish attaches on contact and slows, then after a delay the shark knocks the target up.
audit.why: Root and knock-up behave differently for everything that matters here: a knock-up is displacement, and the fish only ever attaches if it physically touches a champion, which is what makes sidestepping it possible in the first place.
audit.corrected: whys[4] rewritten to 'sidestep the fish before the shark erupts, as it sticks only on contact'.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] describes Seastone Trident as applying 'poison stacks'. Riot's text describes a bleed — magic damage over several seconds — with no stacking mechanic.
audit.why: Flagged as a suspect name by the packet, but the ability NAME is right; the mechanic attached to it is what is wrong.
audit.corrected: 'Land autos with Seastone Trident's bleed damage up close'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Charm stops Urchin Strike, which is a dash and therefore a movement ability.
audit.why: Ahri's E 'instantly stops movement abilities'. Urchin Strike is his only gap-closer that covers ground toward you (Playful/Trickster is 400 and largely defensive), so charm held for the Q is the mechanical answer to his engage rather than a general 'hold charm' instruction.
audit.corrected: Written into winCon, breakdown.carry and dosFull[0].d.

notes: Both packet suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES on the name itself — 'Seastone Trident' and 'Chum the Waters' are correct — but the Seastone Trident line attached the wrong mechanic (poison stacks; it is a bleed), which is fixed. DERIVED-FLAG MISFIRES NOT WRITTEN: the brief tags both Playful/Trickster (E) and Chum the Waters (R) with 'grounding: shuts off enemy dashes', but neither of Riot's descriptions contains any grounding language — E is a hop plus a slam, R is a slow plus a knock-up. Per the calibration rule I trusted the descriptions and wrote nothing claiming Fizz can shut off Spirit Rush. If that is genuinely wrong it matters a lot for this specific matchup (it would mean Ahri cannot dash out of his all-in at all), so it is listed as unverified rather than asserted. Level chart: the full layer disagreed with the content layer and the packet on six of seven rows, including handing Level 1 to Fizz; six side flips proposed as one atomic group, with no matching win[] edits because win[] already reads correctly. | COHERENCE: 1 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it. Chart authority is an open question, so the label was reverted rather than the prose rewritten. Re-propose only as a side+why pair.
